question: Can the already-existing final held-out rain x local-history gating null reproduce the previously established higher-order within-taxon concentration of route-new multi-site activity?
population: Exactly the 2,916 physically stable, strictly-prior-history-eligible pairs across 439 routes used by the existing final cross-fit rain-by-memory gating null.

endpoint.route_new_species_gain: Number of route-new taxa in the wet survey.

null: Exactly the already-existing final null: strictly-prior species x SiteID probabilities + a=0.75 dry persistence + route-cross-fit species-specific rainfall shifts + one route-cross-fit global rain x centered local-memory gate on currently silent cells + pair-level wet-incidence magnitude matching.
conditioning: Across 1,000 simulations of the existing final null, regress higher_order_beta on route_new_species_beta and extra_stop_beta. Compare the observed conditional residual with the simulated residual distribution.
primary_rule: Residual higher-order dependence survives the final null only if the observed conditional residual exceeds the upper 95% null-residual bound.
interpretation: Pass means the existing final held-out species + prior-history + dry-persistence + rain-by-history gate still does not reproduce the observed higher-order concentration after first-order recruitment and spread are conditioned.
Fail means this strongest pre-existing null is sufficient for the higher-order endpoint; the manuscript must not claim higher-order dependence beyond that final null.
This is an endpoint audit of an already-existing null, not a new mechanism model.
No literal synchrony, movement, social facilitation, hydrological connectivity, causal rainfall, or universal mechanism is inferred.
No statistic, subset, fitted lambda, cross-fit rule, null construction, tail or threshold may change after endpoint readback.
